# 天气·水·天象 {.unnumbered}

### Between Storm and Starlight

The morning broke [dim]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dim · adj. 暗淡的, 昏暗的, 不明亮的; 隐约的, 模糊不清的; &amp; 变暗淡, 变模糊 DIMabbr…"}, a pewter sky that swallowed every [ray]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ray · n. 光束, 光线; 射线; 微量, 丝毫 Ray雷"} before it could reach the ground. Overnight [hail]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hail · n. 冰雹；致敬；招呼；一阵; 招呼；猛发；致敬；向...欢呼；使像下雹样落下; 下雹；招呼; 欢迎；万岁"} had left the courtyard [awash]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="awash · adj. 与水面齐平的, 刚被水覆盖的; 很多的"}, and now a fine [mist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mist · n. 薄雾; 视线模糊不清; &amp; 蒙上薄雾, 模糊"} drifted in from the valley, turning the tree-line [misty]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="misty · adj. 模糊的；有雾的"} and soft. A low [haze]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="haze · n. 疑惑；阴霾；薄雾; 使变朦胧；使变糊涂; 变朦胧；变糊涂"} settled over the hills — the kind of [hazy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hazy · adj. 朦胧的；模糊的；有薄雾的"} half-light that makes distances impossible to judge. [Drips]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="drips · n. 水滴; 滴下；充满；给…打点滴"} fell from the eaves in slow, uneven rhythm, each one landing in a puddle gone [soggy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="soggy · adj. 浸水的；透湿的；沉闷的"} from the night. The air was [muggy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="muggy · adj. 闷热的；潮湿的"}, heavy with the smell of wet earth, though a [chill]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="chill · vt. &amp; 变冷, 变凉; 寒冷, 寒气; 寒颤, 发冷 CHILLCHILL语言"} still clung to the shadows where the warmth had not yet reached.

By midday the sky changed its mind. The clouds tore open and sunlight hit the wet stones with a sudden [blaze]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blaze · n. 火焰, 烈火; 光辉, 闪耀; 迸发, 爆发; 猛烈地燃烧; 发光, 照耀"}, its [fiery]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="fiery · adj. 燃烧般的；热烈的，炽烈的；暴躁的"} edge hard to look at straight on. The [dazzle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dazzle · n. 耀眼的光；灿烂; 使……目眩；使……眼花; 炫耀；眼花缭乱"} lasted only minutes before a [noser]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="noser · n. 强烈逆风"} rolled in off the ridge — a strong headwind that scattered the [fumes]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="fumes · n. 烟气；激动；空想的事物; 蒸发；冒烟；发怒"} of chimney smoke sideways and made the [lamp]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lamp · n. 灯；照射器; 照亮; 发亮"} in the window gutter and [blur]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blur · vt. 涂污；使…模糊不清；使暗淡；玷污; 沾上污迹；变模糊; 污迹；模糊不清的事物"}. Then came [sleet]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sleet · n. 雨夹雪或雹; 下雨夹雪；下冻雨"}, quick and mean, rattling the glass before the temperature lifted and slow [thaws]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="thaws · n. 融雪; 使融解，暖和"} turned the sleet to cold rain. Down in the creek the current quickened; [eddies]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="eddies · n. 旋涡；涡流; 使起旋涡；起旋涡"} spun in the shallows, pulling leaves in tight circles. A [breeze]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="breeze · n. 微风；轻而易举的事；煤屑；焦炭渣；小风波; 吹微风；逃走"} picked up behind the squall, and the [flush]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="flush · v. 脸红，发红; 冲; 冲洗净，冲洗; 冲走; 潮红，脸红; 一阵强烈情感，一阵激情; 冲; 同花的一手…"} of cold air finally broke the [muggy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="muggy · adj. 闷热的；潮湿的"} weight that had pressed on the valley all morning.

By dusk the storm was spent. In the west, the last clouds caught a [glow]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="glow · vi. 燃烧；发炽热；烧红; 脸红，身体发热; 光亮，光辉; 脸红，发热; 热情；强烈的感情"} from the sun already gone. A solar [flare]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="flare · vt. 使张开；使闪耀；用发光信号发出；使外倾; 闪耀，闪光；燃烧；突然发怒; 闪光，闪耀；耀斑；照明弹；爆…"} had been forecast, and sure enough, the upper atmosphere began to [flare]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="flare · vt. 使张开；使闪耀；用发光信号发出；使外倾; 闪耀，闪光；燃烧；突然发怒; 闪光，闪耀；耀斑；照明弹；爆…"} in pale curtains of green. Then — low and unhurried on the eastern horizon — a [comet]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="comet · n. 彗星"} appeared, its tail a slow brushstroke across the dark. Someone ran out with a bucket of water to [douse]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="douse · vt. 浇水在…上; 熄灯〔火〕"} the bonfire; it hissed and died, and we stood in the sudden quiet, watching a sky so clear it felt borrowed. The [haster]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="haster · n. 哈士德风暴"} that had rattled the shutters at noon was now only a memory of cold.

### When the Sky Holds Nothing Back

The morning began with a low [rumble]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rumble · n. 隆隆声, 辘辘声; 发出隆隆声, 发出辘辘声"} rolling across the hills — not yet rain, but a warning. By midday the air had turned [sultry]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sultry · adj. 闷热的；狂暴的；淫荡的"}, the kind of wet, clinging heat that makes every breath an effort. Overhead, the sky was [overcast]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="overcast · adj. 阴暗的；愁闷的；阴天的; 使沮丧；包缝；遮蔽"}, a flat grey lid pressing down on the valley. On the ridge, a few [sunlit]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sunlit · adj. 阳光照射的；被日光照射了的"} patches still broke through, their [radiance]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="radiance · n. 发光;光辉; 辐射; 欣喜的神色"} flickering like a [glimmer]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="glimmer · n. 微光；闪光；少许; 闪烁；发微光"} of hope before clouds swallowed them whole. Where sunlight did reach the wet asphalt, it [glitter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="glitter · vi. 闪烁；闪光; 闪光；灿烂"}ed briefly, and the shallow puddles [shimmer]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="shimmer · vi. 闪闪发光；发微光"}ed in the shifting light.

Then the [monsoon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="monsoon · n. 季候风；雨季；季风"} arrived in earnest. [Raindrop]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="raindrop · n. 雨滴；雨点"}s the size of coins hammered the earth; within minutes the trail was [drenched]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="drenched · adj. 湿透的；充满的; 浸湿；强使服药；覆盖"}, every leaf [dripping]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dripping · n. 滴,滴下,滴下物,油滴"}. The river, already swollen, began to [overflow]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="overflow · vt. &amp; 溢出；淹没; 充满; 溢出; 溢出物; 容纳不下的人"} its banks, threatening to [inundate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inundate · vt. 泛滥；淹没；浸水；扑来"} the lower fields. A [riptide]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="riptide · n. 激流；洪涛"} churned at the river bend where the current folded back on itself, forming a tight [vortex]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vortex · n. 涡流；漩涡；旋风；中心"} that swallowed a floating branch whole. Farther upstream, [sleeting]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sleeting · v. 下雨夹雪"} rain mixed with the downpour, coating the higher rocks in grey slush. [Moisture]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="moisture · n. 潮湿；水分；降雨量；湿度"} hung in the air long after the worst had passed, and the [iciness]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="iciness · n. 冰冷的性质,冰冷,如冰"} of the wind off the peaks cut straight through wet clothing.

The following week swung to the opposite extreme. A [blazing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blazing · adj. 燃烧的；强烈的；闪耀的; 非常; 燃烧；闪耀；迸发；公开"} sun turned the scrubland into a [torrid]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="torrid · adj. 晒热的；热情的"} expanse; by noon the ground was close to an [inferno]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inferno · n. 阴间，地狱 Inferno胺吸磷"}, the soil cracked and pale. The heat seemed to [scorch]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="scorch · vt. 烧焦；使枯萎；挖苦; 烧焦；枯萎; 烧焦；焦痕"} every blade of grass it touched, leaving behind a brown, brittle memory of green. A [blizzard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blizzard · n. 暴风雪; 暴风雪似的一阵;大量"} of dust spiraled up from the dry riverbed — a [meteoric]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="meteoric · adj. 流星的；疾速的；大气的"} gust that arrived without warning and vanished just as fast. By late afternoon a [blackout]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="blackout · n. 断电;停电; 新闻封锁; 灯火管制; 暂时性眼前昏黑;突然发昏; 停止; 不透光窗罩〔窗帘〕"} rolled through the town below when lightning struck the substation; for an hour the valley sat in an eerie, [glowing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="glowing · adj. 热烈赞扬的,热情洋溢的; 夸奖；美言；赞美; 热情洋溢地"} dusk that was neither day nor dark. At last the clouds broke, and a [sunshiny]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sunshiny · adj. 阳光照耀的,晴朗的,向阳极好的"}, [swelter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="swelter · n. 闷热；热得难受; 被暑气所苦；热得难受; 使闷热；使中暑"}-free evening settled in — golden, still, and mercifully brief.

### When the Storm Passed and the Stars Appeared

The [meteorologist]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="meteorologist · n. 气象学者"} on duty had warned of [inclemency]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inclemency · n. 险恶,严酷"} since dawn, and by afternoon the sky delivered on every threat. A [hurricane]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hurricane · n. 飓风, 旋风"} tore in from the coast without ceremony, its [whirlwind]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="whirlwind · n. 旋风"} arms sweeping rooftops and uprooting palms. The [sweltering]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="sweltering · adj. 闷热的; 热得没气力的"} heat that had pressed down all week vanished in minutes, replaced by a [drenching]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="drenching · n. 湿透"} that left the streets [inundated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inundated 洪泛的"}. Gutters became rivers; car parks turned into shallow seas. Where the current met a bend in the road, a slow [whirlpool]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="whirlpool · n. 漩涡"} spun debris in lazy circles. The town's fire crew reached for every [extinguisher]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="extinguisher · n. 熄火者，扑火者；消火者；消火器；熄火器，灭火器"} they owned, not for flames but to clear pressure from flooded pumping stations — a strange, desperate image in the middle of so much water.

By nightfall the worst had passed, though the ground remained [stone-cold]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stone-cold · adj. 冰冷如石的"} and sodden. A desert traveller elsewhere might have called the remaining gusts a [willy-willy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="willy-willy · n. ①畏来风②沙漠旋风"} — nothing more than a sand-devil — but here it still carried a bite. The [meteorologic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="meteorologic · adj. 气象的,气象学的"} models had tracked the storm's [stratospheric]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stratospheric · adj. 同温层的"} origins accurately enough; what no model captured was the particular quality of the [twilight]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="twilight · n. 黄昏，暮色；衰退期，朦胧状态 虚幻的；模糊的，朦胧的"} that followed: the sky a bruised violet, every puddle [glistening]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="glistening · adj. 闪耀的,反光的"} as though lit from below. [Precipitation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="precipitation · n. 匆促，仓促，鲁莽; 沉淀，析出; 降落；某地区降雨等的量"} totals broke records for the month, and the slow [inundation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="inundation · n. 淹没，泛滥; 洪水; 扑来；压倒"} of the lower valley would take days to drain.

Later, a small group climbed the ridge for an evening of [stargazing]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stargazing · n. 耽于幻想"}. The washed air had stripped away every trace of haze, and [constellation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="constellation · n. 星座; 一群杰出人物"} after [constellation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="constellation · n. 星座; 一群杰出人物"} emerged with unusual sharpness — Scorpius low on the horizon, Orion just clearing the treeline. Someone mentioned [interplanetary space]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="interplanetary space 行星际空间；太空"} in the casual way people do when the sky suddenly feels less abstract, its distances more real than the flood-line still visible on the garden wall below.
